title: PEP 701 nested f-string text is treated as approved assignment rows
symptom: A Python 3.12+ f-string containing a nested triple-quoted string with the same quote style can have literal string-content lines classified as simple assignment rows. The reproduction contains `text = f"""{ """`, followed by `a = 1`, `longer = 2`, `third = 3`, then `""" }"""`. The real public `align --dry-run --json` reported `ok=true`, `fixedPoint=true`, `parserChecked=true`, and the approved `py-simple-assignments` rule, while proposing whitespace edits to the outer f-string line and two lines that are bytes inside the nested literal. Dry-run did not modify the original file; no actual write is claimed.

rootCause.summary: The prior quote masker could mistake a nested same-delimiter string inside a PEP 701 formatted string for the outer boundary, exposing literal content to an approved assignment table. Candidate v2 retains original-source parser-owned ranges, UTF-16/newline preservation and the independent AST guard, and fixes raw align-only invalid-source JSON without guessed ranges. Focused and full checks plus the Opus fix-only review passed; public approvals were not expanded.

requestedOutcome: For PEP 701 nested same-delimiter f-strings, preserve the exact runtime string value and do not classify replacement-field literal lines as assignment rows. If the syntax cannot be decomposed safely, refuse conservatively in both preview and write pipelines.
decisions: Keep public approvals separate from parser/mask correctness; this defect does not authorize changing the approved preset.
Do not claim a destructive write from the observed dry-run. Verification must include the approved public write path on isolated copies and prove exact original/runtime value preservation.

actions.description: Use parser-owned Python formatted-string ranges from original source with UTF-16 offsets and retained physical line separators; keep the ordinary no-prefix fast path and the independent AST guard for changed writes.
Handle SyntaxWarning and DeprecationWarning without accepting arbitrary stderr, and return a bounded changed/refused JSON result for pre-existing invalid syntax without writing.
Protect uppercase formatted-string prefixes on older STRING-token runtimes and accept only exact LF/CRLF AST protocol markers.
Return controlled structured refusal for invalid Python containing an f/t-string prefix without guessed ranges; preserve fail-closed handling for other parser/protocol errors.
Complete the v2 frozen checks and required fixed-model Opus fix-only review before closure; both are now recorded as passed.

Make raw no-write Python align/check return the structured invalid-source result for f/t-prefix probe matches, including plain strings that accidentally match the quick probe; preserve unchanged bytes and fail-closed errors; regression and review evidence are recorded for candidate v2.
